item.title: What redistricting means for Tennessee voters
item.description: What happens when Congressional district lines are redrawn, splitting neighbors and grouping them with people far away
item.dc:creator: Ally J. Levine, Bianca Flowers, David Hood-Nuño
item.content:encoded: It’s a political fault line that leaves neighbors onboth sides with less say. 9th District5th District The street outside Tammy Jo O'Neal's home has become a political boundary with big implications. The city of Memphis used to sit almost entirely in one congressional district. The new map splits O'Neal from neighbors across the street, each now belonging to districts with voters halfway across the state who have different needs and interests. O'Neal sees the new map as more than a split block. “There's this divide that's happening in our lives,not just in our districts.” District 5 District 9 Tammy Jo O’Neal sits for a portrait on the front porch of their home on Elzey Ave in Memphis, Tennessee, US, July 29, 2026. REUTERS/Seth Herald A citydivided By Bianca Flowers , David Hood-Nuño and Ally J. Levine Published Oct. 17, 2026 6:00 a.m. EDT What happens when congressional district lines are redrawn, splitting neighbors and grouping them with people far away Four years before the Memphis redistricting, Republicans used a similar strategy in drawing new maps for Nashville. They split the city, which had voted overwhelmingly Democratic for roughly 70 years, into three broader districts where Republicans can now easily prevail. Battles over redistricting have long been intertwined with racism and political power, particularly in southern states like Tennessee. Sixty-four years ago, a federal court found Tennessee diluted voting power in urban areas where majority Black voters lived and ordered the legislature to redraw its congressional districts. For decades, the Voting Rights Act of 1965 was a powerful tool for Black voters, particularly in the South, to challenge discrimination and protect political power among people of color to elect representatives who would advocate for their communities. The act significantly increased Black and Hispanic representation in Congress by curtailing certain redistricting practices, including splitting people of color among many districts or concentrating them in some districts to limit their impact in others. But those protections have been steadily weakened. In 2013, when Democrat Barack Obama was president, the Supreme Court’s decision on the Alabama case Shelby County v. Holder gutted a provision requiring federal approval before states change voting laws or political maps. In April, the court narrowed the Voting Rights Act further in Louisiana v. Callais , making it harder to challenge new maps that dilute the voting power of communities of color. The court essentially required such challenges to prove that districts were drawn intentionally to discriminate on the basis of race, and not for other reasons. Republicans argue their redistricting in Tennessee and elsewhere is about party politics, not race. They point out that Democrats regularly redraw districts in states they control to give their party easier election wins. Democrats have done the same in California, for example, said Steve Hickey, chair of the Republican Party in Williamson County, a popular suburban area south of Nashville. “This is part of a bigger game being played nationally, and I don’t think it’s fair to say that this was done to gut” the Voting Rights Act, he said. Redistricting in the United States is generally controlled by state legislatures, which adjust voter maps after the once-a-decade census. Both parties have historically used the process to help their candidates win future elections. In 2025, at the urging of President Donald Trump, Texas launched an unusual mid-decade redistricting drive as part of a broader Republican push to gain congressional seats in half a dozen states, including Tennessee. Democrats responded with their own partisan redistricting in California and attempts that faltered in other states. Civil rights activists say Tennessee’s congressional districts, all of which currently favor Republicans, are now a testing ground for dismantling voting rights protections across the United States. “This lack of competition spills over and has racial implications,” said John Geer, a political science professor at Vanderbilt University who conducts polling in Tennessee. Reuters sought to quantify the impact of redistricting on the voters of Tennessee, examining public funding, demographics and socioeconomic factors to show why it’s important to residents when a city is split up like this. MemphisDistrict 9Suburbs of NashvilleDistrict 5District 8District 9 Population by race, one dot per person Black residents White residents Other races and ethnicities Memphis has the largest Black population in Tennessee. The city of some 630,000 people is 63% Black. Memphis accounted for 78% of the former District 9’s population, making it the only majority-Black district in the state. Earlier this year, the Tennessee legislature drew new district lines, splitting Memphis and its Black communities into three separate districts. The pieces of the city are now grouped with rural and suburban Tennesseans in districts that reach halfway across the state. Note: “White” and “Black” are non-Hispanic. “Other races and ethnicities” combines Hispanic or Latino residents of any race with the non-Hispanic categories Asian alone, American Indian and Alaska Native alone, Native Hawaiian and Other Pacific Islander alone, Some Other Race alone, and Two or More Races. Sources: US Census Bureau (2020 census redistricting data; TIGER/Line boundaries); Tennessee Comptroller of the Treasury (2026 districts); All About Redistricting, Loyola Law School (2022 districts); State of Tennessee and the City of Memphis Engineering Division (city limits); Tennessee Department of Transportation (roads) Reuters spoke to more than 35 redistricting scholars, political analysts, civic leaders, political candidates and voters about the consequences of redistricting for the most vulnerable communities in Tennessee’s two biggest cities. Cities faced the biggest impact because rural areas were already represented by a Republican and continue to be so after the redistricting, albeit in districts with different demographics. Before redistricting, both Nashville and Memphis were overwhelmingly Democratic districts in an otherwise Republican state. In 2024, District 9, including most of Memphis, went 71% for Democrat Steve Cohen. In 2020, Jim Cooper, a Democrat, ran unopposed in Nashville’s District 5, winning more than 99% of votes cast. In 2022, the new District 5 flipped, with the Republican candidate winning 57%. Tennessee’s new maps have combined city, suburban and rural populations that have widely varying needs and political preferences. The residents of Nashville and Memphis, for instance, are far more likely to struggle with poverty, housing, public safety and related issues. Residents there could now struggle to elect Congress members who prioritize policies to address these issues, according to Odessa Kelly, executive director of Stand Up Nashville, a nonprofit community organization that advocates for racial and economic equality. She said Black voters in Nashville no longer felt they had someone to stand up for them in Congress, from federal funding going to the city to critical votes on bills that directly affect city residents. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention developed the Social Vulnerability Index to gauge how well a community can withstand and recover from an emergency, and to identify which communities may need the most support. Shelby County, home to Memphis, ranks among the most vulnerable of Tennessee’s 95 counties on various indicators such as housing cost burden and lack of access to a vehicle. Memphis, Nashville residents rank higher in social vulnerability A US government index compares Tennessee communities on socioeconomic and demographic factors gauging their resilience to unexpected hardships. 25th 50th 75th 100th percentile Lower vulnerability Higher vulnerability Shelby County (Memphis) Minority status Racial or ethnic minority 100 Davidson County (Nashville) Housing and transportation In structures of 10+ units 97 No vehicle available 94 More people than rooms 60 Lives in group quarters 56 Mobile homes 0 Household characteristics Aged 17 and under 97 Single-parent household 96 Speaks English less than well 91 With a disability 9 Aged 65 and over 5 Socioeconomic status Housing cost burdened 100 Unemployed 86 No health insurance 76 Below 150% of poverty 50 No high school diploma (25+) 16 0 Chart showing where Shelby County and Davidson County rank among Tennessee’s 95 counties on 16 measures of the CDC’s Social Vulnerability Index, grouped into four themes, on a scale from the 0 to the 100th percentile with the other 93 counties as faint ticks. Both rank high on most measures — Shelby at the 100th percentile for racial or ethnic minority share and housing cost burden, Davidson at the 100th for apartments in large buildings and for people who speak English less than well. Both drop to the middle or bottom on poverty, the 50th percentile for Shelby and the 23rd for Davidson, and on residents aged 65 and over. Source: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry Social Vulnerability Index 2022 In 2024, just over a third of Tennessee voters picked Democratic presidential candidate Kamala Harris, and in 2020, Democrats won two congressional seats out of the state’s nine, carrying Nashville and Memphis. Now, every congressional district in Tennessee is considered “safe” for Republicans. Sandi Wells, a self-described “very conservative” voter from Williamson County, just outside Nashville, said it was “kind of odd” to group Memphis in the same district with parts of Williamson County 200 miles away. But she rejected the notion that districts should be drawn to protect Black voting power. “I don’t think we should have districts that are based on race,” she said. “I mean, that’s just ridiculous for anyone to even think that we should have that.” Shane Tinnin, a 52-year-old small business owner who maintains homes in both cities and has voted mostly for Democrats, understands that parties seek political power through redistricting but called the Memphis maps a particularly striking setback for Black political power. “In Nashville, it seemed really more like this is a political move,” he said, noting that it was not a Black-majority city. “When you do it in Memphis, where it’s an even more liberal district, but also a predominantly Black district, it just feels especially egregious to me.” Odessa Kelly, executive director at Stand Up Nashville, points to topics of focus for her and her team at a meeting in July. REUTERS/Seth Herald Volunteers for The Equity Alliance canvass through neighborhoods in Memphis to do “accountability” door knocks to speak with residents about elected officials following the GOP-led effort to redistrict the city. REUTERS/Seth Herald Securing funding Reuters examined how Nashville’s redistricting has impacted community project funding, under which lawmakers can seek federal money for local projects. Previously known as earmarks, community project funds returned to Congress with a more transparent process in fiscal year 2022 after a decade-long moratorium. A Reuters analysis found a dramatic shift in funding for Nashville after the city was split among three districts. Jim Cooper, a Democrat, steered most of the old 5th District’s project funding to Nashville in fiscal years 2022 and 2023. In the years since, only a small share of funding has gone toward projects in the city, including fiscal year 2027 requests still pending before Congress. Funding can vary greatly between representatives. Only John Rose, who currently represents the 6th District, has requested funding among the three members whose districts included Nashville after redistricting. Matt Van Epps and Andy Ogles have not pursued community project funding for their districts at all, arguing against such spending on principle. All three did not provide a comment or did not respond to a request to comment. Total Community Project Funding for districts that include Nashville After FY2023 FY2024 $18 mln $21 mln $2.5 mln Not Nashville $18 mln Nashville Nashville $3 mln $15.5 mln Before Two flow diagrams comparing Community Project Funds before and after redistricting. In the year before, when Nashville sat in a single district, District 5 received $18 million and $15.5 million of it went to Nashville, with $2.5 million going elsewhere. In the year after, with Nashville divided across three districts, Districts 5, 6 and 7 received $21 million between them but only $3 million reached Nashville, while $18 million went to areas outside the city. Note: Data show the total funding for districts that include Nashville. Before the 2022 redistricting, Nashville was contained in District 5. After, it was split between Districts 5, 6 and 7. Source: US Government Accountability Office The shift away from community funding jeopardized future funding for projects like public housing, healthcare centers, buildings for the two historically Black colleges in the city and public transportation in Nashville. For Memphis, a similar decline in earmark funding would be a big loss. Since 2022, District 9 Representative Steve Cohen, a Democrat, pulled in $52.6 million for projects based in Memphis, according to figures published by the US Government Accountability Office and the US House Committee on Appropriations. That’s 83% of all the community project funding for District 9 in that period. District 7 State capitol District 6 State House of Representatives The Tennessee State Capitol building and Legislative Plaza, which is undergoing construction. REUTERS/Seth Herald Another important role for a member of Congress is to act as a middleman between people in their district and the government, helping negotiate the bureaucracy of Washington. When Cooper represented Nashville, he fielded calls about immigration paperwork, passports, Medicare, Social Security checks and more, said Tennessee State Senator Charlane Oliver, who worked as a community liaison and communications staffer in Cooper’s congressional office from 2017 to 2019. “He would show up to the cookout, the fish fry, the parades, the meetings and the galas,” she said. That kind of interaction is harder if the representative does not have a local office. When Nashville was split, only one representative, Mark Green of District 7, kept an office near the center of the city. That office was closed when Van Epps took over the seat in 2025, leaving no offices within the city limits. Constituents in Nashville have to drive 36 miles on average to visit a congressional district office, a Reuters analysis found, compared with less than 10 miles when Cooper represented Nashville, the seat of Davidson County. Average trip to Congressional district office District 5 +39 miles after District 6 +17 mi District 7 +16 mi 0 10 20 30 40 50 miles 9 miles before redistricting A chart of the average driving distance for Nashville residents to their closest congressional district office, shown for each of the three districts the city is now split among. A dark bar common to all three marks the 9-mile average from when Nashville sat in a single district, flagged on the scale as “9 miles before redistricting.” A lighter bar extends past it to each district’s new average: District 5 adds 39 miles, reaching about 47; District 6 adds 17, reaching about 25; and District 7 adds 16, reaching about 24 miles. Note: Data shows the average driving distance for Nashville residents in each district to their closest district office. District 7’s offices are those open under Rep. Matt Van Epps, who won the seat after Mark Green resigned in 2025. Green kept an office in downtown Nashville; which put District 7’s average at 5 miles. That office no longer exists. Source: Reuters analysis of congressional district office locations Van Epps and the other two Republicans running this year in Nashville districts, Johnny Garrett and Charlie Hatcher, did not respond to Reuters requests for interviews for this story. Most city buses don’t operate far enough outside the city to visit a congressional district office in Cookeville, more than an hour’s drive away. Kyle Cook, who works in the public library, said Cooper’s office used to be just upstairs from his own in downtown Nashville. “Now, if I wanted to advocate just as a regular citizen for better busing, I would have to call this office in Cookeville and it’s just not the same kind of relationship,” Cook said. Who speaks for Memphis? Cohen represented Memphis for 19 years but stood down when new maps were passed, saying “these districts were drawn to beat me.” State Representative Justin Pearson, a progressive Democrat, is campaigning to represent the 9th District. Pearson gained national attention in 2023 when he was temporarily expelled from the Tennessee House, for what Republicans described as a breach of decorum when he joined a protest on gun control . Polls show him trailing Brent Taylor, a Republican state senator endorsed by President Donald Trump. But Pearson said Tennessee was “not a lost cause” for Democrats. In an interview with Reuters, Pearson described the Memphis redistricting as “one of the most significant political deprivations of Black political power and accessibility to the ballot since the end of Reconstruction in Tennessee.” Tennessee State Representative Justin Pearson stands for a portrait in the Cooper Young neighborhood in Memphis. REUTERS/Seth Herald Taylor has defended redistricting efforts in Tennessee as a “compliance measure” in response to the 2026 US Supreme Court ruling that he says prohibits the consideration of racial data when redrawing political boundaries. Asked about his top priorities in such a diverse district spanning downtown Memphis to rural Fayette County, Taylor pointed to inflation. “Everybody feels the pain right now,” he said. “When I filled up my car the other day, it was $112. People feel the pinch at the gas pump. They feel higher prices when they go to the grocery store. Everything we do costs more.” Civil Miller-Watkins, an eighth-grade math teacher in Fayette County who was drawn into District 9 and plans to vote for Pearson, said the needs of voters in her area differ from those in Memphis. Rural voters worry about access to broadband, ambulances, grocery stores and schools, she said. “All of these interests are very legitimate,” Miller-Watkins said. “But I don’t know if any community can say they’re going to have effective representation.” Pearson, the Democrat, says he’s campaigned in 15 counties that now come under the district and economic hardship is the common thread. “That’s hurting people who are working class in Memphis, just like it’s hurting farmers in Savannah, Tennessee,” he said. “We have a lot more in common.” Urban 96% Suburban 4% Shelby County 737,000 people live in an urban county in District 9 Tipton County 31,000 live in a suburban county District 9 After Urban 35% Suburban 27% Memphis Nashville Williamson 107k Shelby 269k people Rutherford 39k Maury 33k Memphis area Small towns 22% Bedford 50k Lincoln 35k McNairy 26k Giles 30k Hardeman 25k Marshall 34k Lawrence 44k Hardin 27k Wayne 16k Moore 7k Rural 16% Before redistricting Fayette 25k Two panels comparing the counties that make up Tennessee’s 9th Congressional District before and after the 2026 redraw, with each county drawn at an area proportional to its population. Before, the district is almost entirely one place: urban Shelby County, home to Memphis, fills the panel with roughly 737,000 people, beside a thin sliver for suburban Tipton County’s ~31,000. After, 767,872 people are spread across 15 counties in four groups. Urban counties make up 35% of the district; suburban counties comprise 27%, small towns 22% and rural counties 16%. Note: Counties are grouped by the National Center for Health Statistics urban–rural classification. “Large central metro” was renamed to “Urban”, “Large fringe metro” to “Suburban”, “Micropolitan” to “Small towns” and “Noncore” was renamed “Rural” in this graphic. Sources: US Census; NCHS Urban-Rural Classification Scheme; Tennessee Comptroller of the Treasury (2026 district); All About Redistricting, Loyola Law School (2022 district) Pearson said he was concerned that some voters were confused about which district they were in and that this could hurt turnout. Pearson’s advocacy for criminal justice reform and affordability has appealed to younger Democratic Party voters like 27-year-old Marko Jankov. But Jankov, who identifies as a Democratic Socialist, lives in a part of Memphis that was moved out of the 9th District and he said he was less motivated to vote for other Democrats when polls showed them unlikely to win. “They want to make it a psychological thing, where you think you can’t win,” Jankov said. The changes are exposing a rural-urban divide. Debby Gould, president of the non-partisan League of Women Voters of Tennessee, said voters of all backgrounds had concerns. “This is a time when we really have to strengthen urban-rural links and to come up with shared values,” she said. “Because rural voters are also feeling left out on this.” Hickey, the Williamson County Republican chair, said it was up to candidates to show they could work for all their constituents: “They’re going to have to put a lot of miles in their car.” Opening photo Elzey Avenue in Memphis, a dividing line between Congressional District 9 and Congressional District 5, following a Republican-led effort to redistrict Memphis. REUTERS/Seth Herald Sources US Census Bureau (2020 Census redistricting data, TIGER/Line); Tennessee Comptroller of the Treasury (2026 congressional districts); All About Redistricting, Loyola Law School (2022 congressional districts); State of Tennessee and the City of Memphis Engineering Division (city limits); Tennessee Department of Transportation (roads). Additional contributions by Travis Hartman, Ben Kellerman and Tiana McGee Edited by Claudia Parsons, Kat Stafford and Julia Wolfe More from Reuters Graphics

item.title: Trump waives many Russia-related sanctions, tariffs before they were to take effect under new law
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Friday that he is waiving many sanctions, restrictions and duties days before they were to take effect under a bill that he signed into law last month.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh, Jasper Ward
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump said on Friday that he is waiving many sanctions, restrictions and duties days before they were to take effect under a bill that he signed into law last month. Trump's executive order comes as he has been warming toward Russia and publicly criticizing Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, including suggesting that Ukraine needs a new leader. The legislation, whose primary backer in Congress was the late Senator Lindsey Graham, would have imposed tariffs of up to 100% within 30 days on all goods brought into the US from the five largest importers of Russian crude oil or gas, as well as any country that knowingly bought oil or gas 30 days after the law was enacted or was among the top five countries helping Russia evade sanctions. Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 in mid-September. "I have submitted to the Congress a certification that the issuance of such a waiver at this time is in the national interests of the United States," Trump said in the order released by the White House on Friday. Countries such as India, which is among the biggest buyers of Russian oil, have raised concerns about the Russia sanctions bill.

item.title: ALCS Game 4 between Guardians, Rays postponed to Saturday
item.description: CLEVELAND -- Day-long rain that turned into soaking showers in the early evening led to the postponement of Game 4 of the American League Championship Series on Friday night.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: CLEVELAND -- Day-long rain that turned into soaking showers in the early evening led to the postponement of Game 4 of the American League Championship Series on Friday night. The Cleveland Guardians lead the Tampa Bay Rays 2-1 in the best-of-seven series, which now will resume Saturday at 8 p.m. A scheduled off-day Sunday has been erased with Game 5 shifted to 5 p.m. that day, also in Cleveland. MLB officials made the decision to postpone the game an hour after its scheduled first pitch of 8:08 p.m. More than a dozen Rays players were working out in the outfield, playing catch in the heavy rain, before the announcement was made. Rays right-hander Nick Martinez (0-0, 4.91 ERA) was scheduled to pitch against Guardians right-hander Shawn Armstrong (0-0, 0.00 ERA). Cleveland had planned on a bullpen game in order to allow Foster Griffin, Parker Messick and ace Gavin Williams to start the final three potential contests. Games 6 and 7 will be hosted by the Rays. It was the latest weather-related disruption to the championship series. Game 3 on Thursday was moved up from an evening start to 1 p.m. due to inclement weather in the forecast. The Guardians prevailed 3-2 to move ahead in the series. --Brian Dulik, Field Level Media

item.title: Bangladesh is battling measles. It's a 'real warning' to other nations
item.dc:creator: Ruma Paul, Jennifer Rigby, Sam Jahan, Zia Chowdhury
item.content:encoded: The parents of Labiba Akter have kept a blue dress once worn by their nine-month-old daughter, who died of measles in June, as a keepsake. They were not told she was eligible for a vaccination before she contracted the disease. REUTERS/Mohammad Ponir Hossain Bangladesh is battling to contain the world’s worst measles outbreak , a crisis exacerbated by weak data, inadequate outreach and vaccination gaps that experts say offers a warning to other nations about the deadly risk of falling immunisation rates. Bangladesh, whose routine vaccination programme faltered in 2025, reported 202,000 suspected measles cases – 22,000 of them laboratory-confirmed – since the start of the outbreak in mid-March to October 9, the World Health Organization said. That’s more suspected cases than any other country this year. So far, 1,147 people have died of the highly contagious disease, with 94% of reported deaths among children under five years old, the WHO said. Bangladesh's experience shows the challenge of containing an outbreak when vaccination coverage falls below 95%, a level the WHO says is needed to prevent outbreaks. Bangladesh almost achieved that in recent years but in 2025 coverage dropped. A Reuters review of WHO documents, alongside interviews with more than a dozen scientists, health workers and officials, shows Bangladesh was also hampered in its emergency response by data that left out millions of children, shortcomings in preparation and a failure to reach enough parents. "This is a real warning to every country," said Mark Jit, a WHO vaccine adviser and professor at the School of Global Public Health at New York University. Preventing an outbreak through vaccinations was easier, cheaper and safer than responding to an emergency, he said. "The response will stop the outbreak eventually, but in the meantime, many will have had measles, and some will have died," he said. Ziauddin Hyder, special assistant on health affairs to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, told Reuters in September the government was doing everything it could to end the outbreak. The government did not respond to further questions sent in October for this article. Amin Mia and Sajina Begum pose with their four-year-old daughter who survived measles. Below, Sajina Begum shows a photo of her husband, daughter and two-year-old son, Arman Hossain, who died of the disease in July. Neither child received a vaccination. REUTERS/Mohammad Ponir Hossain REUTERS/Mohammad Ponir Hossain ‘THEY CAME ONLY AFTER I BURIED MY SON’ In the northeast Sylhet region, one of the worst-hit areas in the nation of 178 million people, two-year-old Arman Hossain died unvaccinated in July, 24 hours after admission to hospital for treatment paid for by selling the family's three-wheeled auto rickshaw. His unvaccinated four-year-old sister survived. His father Amin Mia, 26, said no health workers came to their remote village in Sylhet to offer vaccinations in time. "They came only after I buried my son," he said. Measles usually kills two or three people in every 1,000 cases, the WHO says, but the disease can be more deadly in poorer nations because of factors such as malnutrition. This is a real warning to every country. Mark Jit, a WHO vaccine adviser In the town of Chhatak, also in the Sylhet region, the daughter of 30-year-old carpenter Humayun Rashid died unvaccinated in June aged nine months. Labiba Akter could have received an inoculation in April when an emergency programme lowered the vaccination age to six months from nine. "No health worker came to tell us," her father said. In May, Health Minister Sardar Md. Sakhawat Husain said the emergency drive had brought cases in hotspots "almost to zero" and the outbreak was under control. Yet in September, Bangladesh reported a daily average of 1,198 new cases of measles, which causes a high fever, cough and telltale rash. That was the highest total since May. The Bangladesh outbreak comes as vaccine hesitancy is rising, particularly in wealthier nations, amid skepticism championed by figures such as US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. In Bangladesh, access to inoculations and awareness are bigger hurdles, experts said. Until recently, Bangladesh had been a vaccination success story. The WHO and the United Nations children’s agency UNICEF estimated that in 2024 it achieved 96% coverage for the first vaccine dose and 93% for the second, which is given to capture the small percentage of children who don't develop immunity after one shot. But that same year, protests erupted that ended 15 years of rule by Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. In the ensuing political turmoil, health workers went on strike, vaccine orders were delayed and follow-up vaccinations that usually accompany routine programmes were disrupted. Nadia Akter Manna, the mother of Labiba Akter, shows a few personal items bought for her daughter before she died. REUTERS/Mohammad Ponir Hossain Humayun Rashid, the father of Labiba Akter, works on his carpentry in September, three months after his daughter's death. REUTERS/Mohammad Ponir Hossain In a report published in July this year, WHO and UNICEF estimated first-dose coverage in 2025 had fallen to 90%, while second-dose coverage was 86%, several percentage points below the 95% needed for herd immunity. The report also raised questions about the quality of official data on vaccinations for measles and other diseases for the years 2023 to 2025. It said preliminary figures sometimes showed numbers of those inoculated exceeded 100% of those targeted, indicating mistakes in counting doses or target numbers. EMERGENCY PROGRAMME MISSED MILLIONS Still, when the measles outbreak erupted, Bangladesh responded swiftly and initially seemed to be winning the battle. An emergency programme was followed by an initial slowdown in new cases after almost 20 million children received a vaccination in April and May. The government said it had covered every child in the target age group of six months to five years. But in reality the programme fell short. This emerged when another routine health intervention in June had a target list with 4 million more children than the measles campaign despite covering the same age group. "There is a gap," prime ministerial adviser Hyder told Reuters on September 14, as measles cases rose again, blaming vaccine hesitancy by parents or child illnesses for keeping kids away. Iqbal and Sharmin wait as their five-month-old son, Esa, receives treatment for measles in the neonatal intensive care unit of a hospital in Narayanganj, Bangladesh, May 11, 2026. REUTERS/Mohammad Ponir Hossain Other challenges have also emerged. Documents detailing meetings in April and August between the government, the WHO and other health partners, reviewed by Reuters and not previously reported, show how efforts to act fast may have led to shortcomings. Minutes from the April 19 meeting outlined how the government opted for just one round of so-called readiness checks before launching its emergency vaccination programme due to time constraints, instead of the typical four rounds. Checks cover everything from ensuring fridges are available for keeping vaccines cool to determining how many children should be vaccinated. The single round of checks suggested most - but not all - districts were ready, according to the minutes. Eight-year-old Masum receives treatment in the overcrowded measles isolation ward of Shahid Shamsuddin Ahmed Hospital in Sylhet, one of the worst-hit areas in Bangladesh's measles outbreak. REUTERS/Mohammad Ponir Hossain The 100-bed Shahid Shamsuddin Ahmed Hospital in the Sylhet region has been overwhelmed by measles cases. REUTERS/Mohammad Ponir Hossain On the day Reuters visited the hospital in September, 178 patients were admitted. REUTERS/Mohammad Ponir Hossain THE POOREST ‘PAY THE PRICE’ "When preparedness checks are not done properly, it is often the poorest and hardest-to-reach children who miss out on vaccination and pay the price," said Professor Mahmudur Rahman, an epidemiologist and chair of Bangladesh's National Verification Committee for Measles and Rubella Elimination. Hyder said the April campaign was launched in four weeks. Yet Tajul Islam Abdul Bari, who led immunisation in Bangladesh until 2017, said campaigns usually demand months of planning. By the August meeting, shortcomings in the rollout were identified. Minutes noted the proportion of children with confirmed measles cases who had not been vaccinated was "virtually unchanged between pre-campaign (82%) and post-campaign (85%) ... underscoring persistent coverage gaps". The WHO did not respond to questions about the April and August meetings. But deputy WHO representative to Bangladesh, Dr Rajesh Narwal, said the WHO was determined to support the government in its goal of vaccinating every child at risk. "Routine immunisation must become more effective and resilient so that these gaps do not develop again," he said. In Sylhet, where official records show 180 children have died, 8 of 16 families Reuters interviewed in September said they had not seen health workers offering vaccinations. At least six families said health workers visited only after a child had died from measles in their community. A measles survivor, two-year-old Al Raiyan Twoha sleeps on his mother Rajia Begum's shoulder in the Sylhet region of Bangladesh. REUTERS/Mohammad Ponir Hossain At the end of September, the government launched a new campaign to target 3.4 million children previously missed. "We will involve people across villages so that no child is left behind," the health minister told a news conference. Yet reaching every child remains a challenge. UNICEF and the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics say as many as 40% of children go unregistered, while government data showed around a third of health worker posts are unfilled. Health experts are also pushing the government to expand the programme to vaccinate children over five. That age group represents a third of measles cases, the WHO says. In addition, scientists in Bangladesh are studying why immunity is waning faster than expected in babies up to six months or so. They are usually still protected by maternal antibodies, experts say. Ensuring prompt medical care is vital, the WHO says, another challenge for Bangladesh as it also fights a dengue epidemic . In September, every ward in Sylhet's 100-bed Shahid Shamsuddin Ahmed Hospital, which is treating measles, appeared overwhelmed. On the day Reuters visited, 178 patients were admitted. The blue dress of measles victim Labiba Akter hangs on a line in the village in Bangladesh’s Sylhet region where her parents live. REUTERS/Mohammad Ponir Hossain

item.title: Anthropic offers Blackstone double-digit yield in chip-financing deal, FT reports
item.description: Anthropic is offering Blackstone a yield of more than 10% to finance its latest chip deal, the Financial Times reported on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Anthropic is offering Blackstone (BX.N) a yield of more than 10% to finance its latest chip deal, the Financial Times reported on Friday. Blackstone funds would invest $9 billion in the debt backed by Anthropic's five-year lease payments on the chips, the report said, citing people familiar with the matter. Reuters could not immediately verify the report.

item.title: テニス＝ジョコビッチ、スイス室内に15年ぶり参戦
item.description: ［１６日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１６日　ロイター］ - 男子テニスで四大大会通算２４勝を誇るノバク・ジョコビッチ（セルビア）が２６日開幕のスイス室内（バーゼル）に主催者推薦で出場することが１６日、決まった。同大会への出場は２０１１年以来１５年ぶりで、４度目となる。

３９歳のジョコビッチは今季、１０月の中国オープンで自身が持つ大会最多優勝記録を更新する７度目のタイトルを獲得した一方、マスターズ上海大会では２回戦でフベルト・フルカチュ（ポーランド）に敗れるなど好不調の波がある。全米オープンでは四大大会で０６年全豪オープン以来となる初戦敗退を喫した。

ジョコビッチは上海大会で敗退した後、今季残りは１１月２─８日のパリ・マスターズと年間成績上位選手によるＡＴＰファイナルにのみ出場する予定だと語っていた。

ジョコビッチは現在、ＡＴＰファイナル出場権を争う年間ポイントランキングで１１位。世界ランキング１位のヤニク・シナー（イタリア）が長引く膝の負傷で今季残りの欠場を決めたため、１７回目の出場を果たすには年間９位以内に入る必要がある。

item.title: テニス＝マスターズ上海大会、メドベージェフとホダルが4強
item.description: ［上海 １６日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［上海　１６日　ロイター］ - 男子テニスのマスターズ上海大会は１６日、シングルス準々決勝を行い、ロシア出身で第５シードのダニル・メドベージェフが第１５シードのトミー・ポール（米国）を６─３、１─６、６─３で下し、準決勝に進出した。

元世界ランキング１位のメドベージェフは１６本のサービスエース、３１本のウィナーを記録。ツアー通算７０回目の準決勝進出を決めた。

２０１９年大会覇者のメドベージェフは今大会で勝ち残っている唯一の歴代優勝者。準決勝では第１２シードのラファエル・ホダル（スペイン）と初対戦する。

２０歳のホダルは第２０シードのカスパー・ルード（ノルウェー）を４─６、６─４、６─３で破り、大会史上最年少の４強入りを果たした。今大会初出場のホダルは４試合連続で第１セットを落としてからの逆転勝利となった。

item.title: Anthropic habría presentado proyecto de ley para frenar modelos de IA que amenacen vidas o causen daños
item.description: La propuesta permitiría al Gobierno de EE.UU. bloquear modelos que impliquen riesgos inminentes de muerte, lesiones o daños superiores a US$1.000 millones, según Politico.
item.dc:creator: Samantha Oltman
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — Según un informe de Politico, Anthropic PBC presentó discretamente a los legisladores estadounidenses su propio proyecto de ley sobre seguridad de la inteligencia artificial, que incluye un plan para regular la seguridad y la protección de la inteligencia artificial. Según Politico, la propuesta sugiere que el Gobierno podría bloquear el lanzamiento de un modelo de IA si se determina que existe un riesgo inminente de que provoque la muerte o lesiones a más de 50 personas o de que cause daños por valor de más de US$1.000 millones. La amenaza debe derivarse de que el modelo cree o lance un arma biológica, de que la IA escape al control humano o de un ciberataque, según informó Politico. Ver más: Anthropic se perfila como la gran apuesta ante la pausa de las salidas a bolsa en EE.UU. El proyecto de ley propone asimismo que evaluadores independientes revisen periódicamente a Anthropic y sus modelos de IA, según ha señalado Politico, citando un borrador al que ha tenido acceso. El borrador recoge muchas de las ideas que Anthropic propuso por primera vez en su Marco de IA Avanzada el pasado mes de junio. El informe no especificó a qué legisladores ni con qué alcance ha presentado Anthropic la propuesta hasta el momento. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

item.title: サッカー＝レアルがリーグ会長の辞任要求、ナチス宣伝手法との比較に反発
item.description: ［マドリード １６日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［マドリード　１６日　ロイター］ - サッカーのスペイン１部レアル・マドリードは１６日、同リーグのハビエル・テバス会長がクラブ経営陣の言動をナチスの宣伝手法に例えたことを受け、同会長の辞任を要求した。

テバス会長は１６日、自身の交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）で、「レアル・マドリードの経営陣は代弁者たちのオーケストラを指揮しており、レアル・マドリードＴＶがそれを主導している」と記した。これは、テバス会長とリーグがレアル・マドリードの利益に反する行動を取っていると指摘した２人のジャーナリストの記事に対する反応だった。

さらに同会長は「彼らのやり方はいつも同じだ。自分たちに都合の良いプレー場面を選び出し、不満を繰り返し、疑念をあおり、敵を指弾する。この手法はナチス・ドイツのゲッベルスが用いた宣伝手法の仕組みをほうふつとさせる」とし、「私が比較したのはあくまで宣伝手法であり、イデオロギーやレアル・マドリードのファンのことではない」と付け加えた。

これに対し、レアル・マドリードは声明で、テバス会長がナチスの宣伝手法を引き合いに出したことは「容認し難く、極めて重大な事態だ」と批判した。「クラブ、経営陣、テレビ局の信用を傷つけようとした。テバス氏の度重なる言動は組織のトップとしての責任を果たす上で不可欠な中立性、敬意、公平性の欠如を示している」とした上で、リーグ会長とスペイン・サッカー連盟副会長を辞任するよう求めた。

item.title: Central rivals Blues, Predators aim to keep building
item.description: Two teams looking to climb the Central Division standings will face off Saturday in Nashville, when the Predators host the St. Louis Blues.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Two teams looking to climb the Central Division standings will face off Saturday in Nashville, when the Predators host the St. Louis Blues. The Blues will wrap up a three-game road trip after they lost 5-4 to the Minnesota Wild on Thursday night. St. Louis scored twice in the final four minutes, including a short-handed goal by Robert Thomas, but coach Jim Montgomery's team could not complete the comeback to force overtime. "Well, 1-1 on a three-game road trip, we got to come out above .500," Montgomery said. "We'll get on the plane, get to Nashville, have a really good practice (Friday) and come out Saturday night with a little more determined effort than we had (Thursday)." Nashville, though, did force the extra session on Thursday. The Predators overcame a 2-0 deficit to San Jose midway through the third period and earned a point thanks to Steven Stamkos' last-second goal, which tied the contest. The Sharks prevailed in the shootout, extending Nashville's winless streak to three games (0-1-2). Nashville has leaned on its veterans, with all five of its leading scorers at least 32 years old. Stamkos, 36, leads the team with four goals and eight points. A two-time Stanley Cup winner with Tampa Bay, Stamkos is now in his third year with Nashville, which has only made the playoffs once in the last four seasons. "I think we're very well aware of where we want to be and how we want to begin the year," coach Andrew Brunette said. "So, I think we're putting a little bit added pressure on ourselves. For sure there's disappointment (with the overtime loss), but we just pick ourselves up and go back to work. You stacked a point out of it, and you build to the next game." Goalie Juuse Saros (2-2-2, 2.95 goals-against average), another Predators veteran, has started six of the team's seven games and stopped 30 shots in the loss to San Jose. The Finnish netminder has allowed just 18 of 187 shots, posting a .904 save percentage. Saros has faced the Blues 24 times over his 12 NHL seasons. He's 10-11-2 with a 3.36 GAA and an .885 save percentage. Nashville may get Mavrik Bourque back in the lineup. The 24-year-old center, acquired in July from the Dallas Stars, has missed the past week due to an upper-body injury, but he was on the ice for practice Friday. St. Louis had its two-game winning streak snapped Thursday, but the Blues have improved offensively, scoring 16 goals over their past three games. Mason McTavish, acquired from Anaheim in June, leads the Blues with five goals and eight points. The 23-year-old center has a five-game point streak, including three goals and an assist in his past two contests. Netminder Joel Hofer (2-2-1, 2.43 GAA) has started both games on the road trip. In eight career games against Nashville, Hofer, 26, is 4-3-0 with a 3.59 GAA and an .865 save percentage. Pavel Buchnevich, who had three assists in the 7-2 win over Ottawa on Tuesday, missed Thursday's game against the Wild due to the birth of his child. It's unclear whether he'll return for Saturday's game. --Field Level Media

item.title: Trump amenaza con usar la “madre de todas las bombas”, pero no serviría contra búnkeres nucleares de Irán
item.description: La bomba no nuclear más grande del arsenal estadounidense podría devastar objetivos en superficie, pero los expertos señalan que no está diseñada para penetrar instalaciones enterradas a gran profundi ...
item.dc:creator: Tony Capaccio
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — La amenaza del presidente Donald Trump de utilizar lo que se conoce como la “madre de todas las bombas” para atacar a Irán podría resultar eficaz a la hora de alcanzar algunos objetivos militares, pero sería de poca utilidad para destruir instalaciones nucleares enterradas a gran profundidad bajo una montaña. El jueves, Trump se negó a descartar el uso de la MOAB —siglas que, en realidad, significan Massive Ordnance Air Blast (explosión aérea de munición masiva)— contra Irán tras las elecciones de mitad de legislatura de Estados Unidos, y más tarde afirmó que las fuerzas estadounidenses podrían tener que “intentarlo” contra una instalación nuclear subterránea situada en Pickaxe Mountain. “La madre de todas las bombas es una bomba enorme, pero no es nuclear”, afirmó Trump en la entrevista concedida a Newsmax. Ver más: Donald Trump dice que EE.UU. no atacará a Irán antes de las elecciones de noviembre El presidente señaló que EE.UU. estaba barajando un futuro ataque contra la montaña Pickaxe de Irán y su complejo de túneles enterrado a gran profundidad bajo la superficie. “Quizá tengamos que ir allí”, afirmó Trump, y “disparar contra ese objetivo”. Aunque Trump no especificó un objetivo para la MOAB de 21 600 libras, los expertos señalaron que este arma no sería la mejor opción contra Irán. La bomba no nuclear más grande del arsenal estadounidense no es, en realidad, un arma de penetración profunda como el Massive Ordnance Penetrator (MOP), lanzada por bombarderos B-2 y que, según Trump, “arrasó” las instalaciones nucleares iraníes en junio de 2025. En cambio, la MOAB es un arma termobárica, también conocida como “bomba de vacío”, que extrae todo el oxígeno del aire circundante para provocar una gran explosión sobre el suelo. Ver más: Rusia, China e Irán usan IA para campañas de desinformación antes de las elecciones de medio mandato de EE.UU. Esto significa que no sería la opción ideal para atacar las instalaciones subterráneas que han complicado y frustrado los intentos del ejército estadounidense de eliminar por completo la amenaza que supone el programa nuclear iraní, según los expertos. Si Trump ordenara nuevos ataques estadounidenses, sería “mucho mejor utilizar bombas antibúnker, ya que están diseñadas específicamente para penetrar bajo tierra antes de explotar”, afirmó Emma Salisbury, investigadora sénior no residente del Programa de Seguridad Nacional del Instituto de Investigación de Política Exterior. No obstante, a pesar de sus limitaciones frente a las instalaciones nucleares subterráneas de Irán, la MOAB podría seguir teniendo un impacto devastador sobre las instalaciones del Cuerpo de la Guardia Revolucionaria Islámica, según Rebecca Grant, analista de poder aéreo del Instituto Lexington. “Tómense en serio las declaraciones de Trump sobre la MOAB”, afirmó. Ver más: Príncipe heredero de Abu Dhabi invierte miles de millones de dólares para eludir control de Irán sobre el estrecho de Ormuz “Se trata de mantener la presión militar sobre el IRGC mientras el bloqueo reduce sus ingresos petroleros”, añadió, refiriéndose al actual bloqueo naval estadounidense de los puertos iraníes. La bomba ya se ha utilizado como amenaza anteriormente. Desarrollada en 2003, antes de la invasión estadounidense de Irak para derrocar a su líder, el entonces secretario de Defensa, Donald Rumsfeld, afirmó que formaba parte de un esfuerzo por ejercer “una presión tan grande que Sadam Husein se viera obligado a cooperar”. El único uso documentado de esta enorme bomba tuvo lugar en abril de 2017, contra un complejo de cuevas y túneles del Estado Islámico de Irak y Siria-Khorasan, en el que, según se informa, murieron unos 36 militantes. Ver más: Presidente de Irán dice ante la ONU que su país no busca armas nucleares, pero defenderá su tecnología A pesar de que se requiere un avión de carga grande, de movimiento más lento y no furtivo para lanzar la MOAB de 30 pies, Grant señaló que cualquier despliegue iría probablemente acompañado de aviones de guerra electrónica que podrían ayudar a protegerla de la defensa aérea y los misiles iraníes. Algunos analistas han cuestionado la utilidad de esta arma contra los principales objetivos restantes en Irán que aún no han sido alcanzados en los más de 13.000 ataques que el Pentágono informó anteriormente en el marco de la guerra contra Irán. “Se trata de un arma termobárica, por lo que su efecto destructivo se basa en la onda de choque de presión”, explicó Doug Barrie, analista de poder aéreo del Instituto Internacional de Estudios Estratégicos. “Es destructiva contra objetivos o estructuras en superficie, pero no contra objetivos enterrados”. -Con la colaboración de Gerry Doyle. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

item.title: Experts divided on whether Dodgers' sweep shifts MLB salary cap fight
item.description: Experts are divided over whether the Los Angeles Dodgers' sweep by the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series will affect Major League Baseball's labor talks, where owners are pushing for a salary cap that players oppose.
item.dc:creator: Rory Carroll
item.content:encoded: Experts are divided over whether the Los Angeles Dodgers' sweep by the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series will affect Major League Baseball's labor talks, where owners are pushing for a salary cap that players oppose. The big-spending Dodgers were thoroughly outplayed by the relentless Brewers, who rank 19th in payroll out of the league's 30 clubs. Milwaukee will return to the World Series for the first time in 44 years after vanquishing the two-time defending champions. Tony Torain, a partner at McDermott Will & Schulte who specializes in labor and employment law, said the result weakens the owners' case that there isn't enough parity in the sport. "I think we'll have a lockout and the league will still try to use that leverage," he said. "But in terms of making the argument for why they think they need a salary cap, the Brewers undercut it. There's definitely leverage on the PA's side," he said, referring to the players' association. He said the union will argue that player development, not payroll, drives winning. He also expects the union to press for higher minimum salaries, an idea it raised early in talks. In their first proposal in May, MLB owners asked for a hard cap of $245.3 million, including player benefits, and a payroll floor of $171.2 million, starting in 2027. The players have long opposed any form of salary cap. The current collective bargaining agreement expires on December 1. Torain said baseball's growing popularity puts added pressure on owners, who have never had a cap in the sport's history. The last time owners pushed for a cap, players went on strike in 1994. The 232-day stoppage forced the cancellation of that year's World Series. "If you have a lockout, it's not on TV, you can't go to the parks, so you're not getting those revenue sources," he said. MESSAGING WIN Bob Dorfman, a San Francisco-based sports marketing analyst, said the Dodgers' playoff exit will change little. "I don't think it's going to change anything that happens for those CBA talks," he said. At most, he said, the sweep is "a messaging win" for the union. He also questioned whether a cap would improve competitive balance, saying attendance, which has risen four seasons in a row, and viewership are strong without one. He agreed that a lockout is likely when the current agreement expires. He said he hopes a stoppage is short, but in a worst case the season could shrink to 70 to 80 games. He said he hopes owners will eventually put off the cap fight for a future contract negotiation. Dorfman said a lockout would anger fans and expects games to be lost, perhaps for a month or two in an optimistic scenario. He said owners tend to win labor fights because they can outlast unions. When reminded that owners failed to win a cap in 1994-95 season, he said, "I hope that happens again."

item.title: ＭＬＢ＝ドジャースのロハスが現役引退、ワールドシリーズ2回制覇
item.description: ［１６日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１６日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）ドジャースに所属するミゲル・ロハス内野手（３７）が１５日、現役引退を表明した。

ドジャースは同日、ナ・リーグ優勝決定シリーズ（７回戦制）第４戦でブルワーズに４─６で敗れ、４連敗で敗退。ワールドシリーズ３連覇の夢が絶たれた試合後、ロハスはチームメートに引退を伝えた。

ロハスは「これで終わりだ。人生、キャリア、野球界での次のステップに進む。今日が選手としてこのユニフォームとスパイクを身に着ける最後の日だった。今はスパイクを脱ぐのが本当につらい」と声を詰まらせながら語った。

ベネズエラ出身のロハスは２０１４年にドジャースでメジャーデビューし、その後マーリンズで８シーズンを過ごし、２３年にドジャースに復帰。２４、２５年のワールドシリーズ連覇を経験した。ＭＬＢ通算１３シーズンで１４０１試合に出場し、打率２割６分、１０４８安打、６１本塁打、３８６打点、６８盗塁を記録した。

２５年のワールドシリーズでは、ブルージェイズとの第７戦で九回に同点本塁打を放ち、優勝に大きく貢献。ドジャース復帰後の４シーズンでは４４６試合に出場し、打率２割６分を記録した。

引退後はドジャースの選手育成部門に加わる予定で、具体的な役職は今後決まる。

item.title: Trump zomba da popularidade do nome Mohammad, comum entre os muçulmanos
item.description: O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, fez uma piada sobre a popularidade do nome Mohammad no mundo muçulmano ao zombar da presidência do Irã durante um discurso de campanha nesta sexta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Steve Holland, Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, fez uma piada sobre a popularidade do nome Mohammad no mundo muçulmano ao zombar da presidência do Irã durante um discurso de campanha nesta sexta-feira. “Sabe, se você tiver dúvidas sobre o nome de alguém do Oriente Médio, basta dizer ‘Mohammad’”, disse Trump à multidão em Dalton, na Geórgia. “Você tem cerca de 65% de chance de acertar. ‘Olá, Mohammad.’ Faço isso há anos. Nunca errei.” Mohammad é um dos nomes masculinos mais comuns entre os muçulmanos, que costumam dar aos filhos o nome do profeta Mohammad, fundador do Islã, conhecido como Maomé no Brasil. Trump fez o comentário enquanto discutia o Irã durante um comício em um hangar no Aeroporto Municipal de Dalton, na Geórgia, onde fez campanha para candidatos republicanos antes das eleições de meio de mandato de 3 de novembro. “O Irã é o único país onde ninguém quer ser presidente”, disse Trump, e então fingiu perguntar a várias pessoas chamadas Mohammad se elas queriam o cargo. Masoud Pezeshkian é presidente do Irã desde 2024. A plateia da Geórgia reagiu com silêncio à piada. Defensores dos direitos humanos e grupos de defesa dos muçulmanos têm criticado repetidamente Trump por uma retórica que, segundo eles, demoniza e ridiculariza muçulmanos, imigrantes e minorias étnicas. Ele intensificou essa retórica durante a campanha para as eleições de meio de mandato, particularmente contra somalis e muçulmanos norte-americanos, incluindo o candidato democrata muçulmano ao Senado dos EUA Abdul El-Sayed e a deputada Ilhan Omar, uma democrata de Minnesota que chegou aos EUA como refugiada somali. Trump reiterou sua promessa de que o Irã nunca teria uma arma nuclear, sete meses depois que os Estados Unidos e Israel lançaram uma guerra contra Teerã com o objetivo, em parte, de paralisar seu programa nuclear. Um relatório anual do Conselho de Relações Islâmico-Americanas, divulgado no início deste ano, atribuiu o aumento da islamofobia nos EUA, em parte, à repressão de Trump à imigração e aos protestos pró-palestinos durante seu segundo mandato.

item.title: EEUU levanta restricciones a aerolíneas mexicanas tras disputa en sector aviación
item.description: Las aerolíneas mexicanas podrán abrir nuevos vuelos a Estados Unidos desde los dos aeropuertos internacionales de Ciudad de México, después de que el Departamento de Transporte de Estados Unidos (DOT por su sigla en inglés) levantara las restricciones impuestas a raíz de las disputas en materia de aviación entre ambos países, dijo el viernes el gobierno mexicano.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Las aerolíneas mexicanas podrán abrir nuevos vuelos a Estados Unidos desde los dos aeropuertos internacionales de Ciudad de México, después de que el Departamento de Transporte de Estados Unidos (DOT por su sigla en inglés) levantara las restricciones impuestas a raíz de las disputas en materia de aviación entre ambos países, dijo el viernes el gobierno mexicano. La decisión permite a las aerolíneas establecer rutas hacia Estados Unidos desde el Aeropuerto Internacional Felipe Ángeles (AIFA) y el Aeropuerto Internacional Benito Juárez de Ciudad de México (AICM), de acuerdo con un comunicado conjunto de las secretarías de Relaciones Exteriores y de Comunicaciones y Transportes. El DOT afirmó que esta medida reflejaba los pasos dados por México para abordar las preocupaciones sobre su cumplimiento de un acuerdo bilateral de transporte aéreo de 2015. El departamento señaló que seguiría exigiendo a las compañías aéreas mexicanas que presentaran los horarios de los vuelos con origen y destino en Estados Unidos y que obtuvieran la autorización para operar servicios con aeronaves de gran tamaño. Un funcionario estadounidense señaló que siguen vigentes otras dos órdenes relacionadas con la controversia y que Washington supervisará de cerca el cumplimiento por parte de México de sus compromisos. El funcionario indicó que la decisión era independiente de una revisión en curso de la Administración Federal de Aviación (FAA por su sigla en inglés) sobre las medidas de supervisión de la aviación en México, llevada a cabo en agosto. La FAA restableció la máxima calificación de seguridad aérea de México en septiembre de 2023, lo que permitió a las aerolíneas mexicanas ampliar las rutas existentes hacia Estados Unidos y poner en marcha nuevos servicios. México había sido degradado en mayo de 2021 después de que el regulador estadounidense determinara que el país no cumplía con las normas internacionales de seguridad aérea. La degradación supuso un duro golpe para las aerolíneas mexicanas, ya que las aerolíneas estadounidenses pudieron hacerse con cuota de mercado. En mayo, el[USN:L6N41I15D TEXT:" secretario de Transporte estadounidense"], Sean Duffy, afirmó que el gobierno mexicano había acordado mejorar el acceso aéreo a Ciudad de México. La administración del presidente estadounidense, Donald Trump, había llegado a un acuerdo con México sobre un plan para abordar las preocupaciones de Estados Unidos respecto al cumplimiento de un acuerdo de transporte aéreo de 2015 entre ambos países, afirmó Duffy. En [USN:L6N3W918R TEXT:"octubre del año pasado"], Estados Unidos congeló la expansión de los servicios de pasajeros y carga de las aerolíneas mexicanas desde esos dos aeropuertos, alegando que México no había cumplido el acuerdo bilateral de aviación desde 2022, cuando rescindió las franjas horarias de las aerolíneas de pasajeros estadounidenses y obligó a las compañías aéreas estadounidenses dedicadas exclusivamente al transporte de carga a trasladar sus operaciones. La decisión del viernes fue bien recibida por las aerolíneas mexicanas; las compañías Viva y Aeroméxico (AERO.MX) señalaron que reforzaría la conectividad aérea entre ambos países.

item.title: サッカー＝フランクフルト3試合ぶり勝利、堂安と小杉はフル出場
item.description: ［１６日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１６日　ロイター］ - サッカーのドイツ１部ブンデスリーガは１６日、１試合を行い、堂安律と小杉啓太がフル出場したアイントラハト・フランクフルトがホームでケルンを１─０で下した。

前半３分に堂安、同９分に小杉がチャンスに絡んだフランクフルトだが、０─０のまま後半へ。それでも、迎えた後半３２分にペナルティーエリア右でパスを受けたユネス・エブヌタリブがシュートを沈め、これを決勝点とした。

フランクフルトは３試合ぶりの勝利。勝ち点８とし、暫定８位に順位を上げた。

item.title: ゴルフ＝原と竹田が首位と3打差の4位、ビュイックＬＰＧＡ
item.description: ［１６日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１６日　ロイター］ - 米女子ゴルフのビュイックＬＰＧＡは１６日、中国・上海の佘山国際ＧＣ（パー７２）で第２ラウンドを行い、原英莉花と竹田麗央が通算３アンダーの４位で並び、首位と３打差につけた。

前日７位の原は５バーディー、５ボギーの７２で回り、３位スタートの竹田は３バーディー、４ボギーの７３とスコアを１つ落とし、原と同じ通算１４１となった。

１２位で出た勝みなみは７８と崩れ、通算４オーバーの３０位に後退。吉田優利は４０位、西郷真央は５１位となった。

前日首位のチェ・ヘジン（韓国）は７４とスコアを２つ落としたものの、通算６アンダーの１３８で単独首位を維持。グレース・キム（オーストラリア）が７２、エイミー・ヤン（韓国）が７１で回り、ともに通算４アンダーの２位につけた。

item.title: サッカー＝上田、ＡＦＣ最優秀国際選手の候補入り
item.description: ［１６日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１６日　ロイター］ - アジア・サッカー連盟（ＡＦＣ）は１６日、２０２６年の年間表彰候補者を発表し、男子の最優秀国際選手賞で日本代表ＦＷ上田綺世（リール）が名を連ねた。

上田は昨季、オランダ１部フェイエノールトで得点王に輝き、今夏のワールドカップ（Ｗ杯）北中米大会でも２得点を記録。韓国代表の黄仁範、前回受賞者の李康仁と共にノミネートされた。

女子の最優秀国際選手賞には長谷川唯が３年連続で候補入り。オーストラリア代表のアランナ・ケネディ、ケイトリン・フォードと選ばれた。

男子の年間最優秀監督賞には、Ｊ１町田の黒田剛監督とＵ─１７（１７歳以下）女子日本代表の白井貞義監督が入った。

男子の年間最優秀若手選手賞では、北原槙、市原吏音、佐藤龍之介の日本人３選手が候補を独占。女子では福島望愛が候補入りした。

表彰式は１１月１９日にタイの首都バンコクで開催され、計１９部門の受賞者が発表される。

item.title: Ukraine-La Moldavie blâme la Russie après que des drones s'écrasent sur son territoire
item.description: Les autorités moldaves ont identifié cinq drones qui se sont écrasé sur son territoire comme étant russes, blâmant vendredi Moscou pour ces incidents.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Les autorités moldaves ont identifié cinq drones qui se sont écrasé sur son territoire comme étant russes, blâmant vendredi Moscou pour ces incidents. Le gouvernement moldave pro-européen, qui espère rejoindre l'Union européenne (UE) d'ici 2030, a critiqué à plusieurs reprises l'invasion de l'Ukraine par la Russie, et a dénoncé des incursions dans son espace aérien. La Moldavie est frontalière de l'Ukraine. Les cinq drones ont pénétré jeudi et vendredi dans l'espace aérien moldave et se sont écrasés sur son territoire, essentiellement dans le nord et l'est du pays, blessant légèrement une personne et provoquant des dégâts. "Ces incidents représentent une menace pour la sécurité de nos citoyens et montre les conséquences directes de la guerre agressive de la Russie contre l'Ukraine sur la stabilité de la région", a dit le ministère moldave des Affaires étrangères dans un communiqué. Le ministère a convoqué l'ambassadeur de Russie en Moldavie, Oleg Ozerov, afin de lui demander des explications après ces incidents.

item.title: Trump mocks popularity of the name Mohammad, common among Muslims
item.description: US President Donald Trump made a joke about the popularity of the name Mohammad in the Muslim world as he mocked Iran's presidency during a campaign speech on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Steve Holland, Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump made a joke about the popularity of the name Mohammad in the Muslim world as he mocked Iran's presidency during a campaign speech on Friday. "You know, if you're in doubt about somebody's name from the Middle East, just say 'Mohammad,'" Trump told a crowd in Dalton, Georgia. "You have about a 65% chance. 'Hello, Mohammad.' I've done it for years now. I've never been wrong." Mohammad is [USN:L5N3N60N8 TEXT:"one of the most common male names"] among Muslims, who often name their sons after the Prophet Mohammad, the founder of Islam. Trump made the comment as he was discussing Iran during a rally in a hangar at Dalton Municipal Airport in Georgia, where he campaigned for Republican political candidates ahead of the November 3 [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"]. "Iran is the only country where nobody wants to be president," Trump said, then pretended to ask several people named Mohammad whether they wanted the job. Masoud Pezeshkian has been president of Iran since 2024. The Georgia crowd gave the joke a muted response. Rights advocates and Muslim advocacy groups have repeatedly criticized Trump for rhetoric that they say demonizes and mocks Muslims, immigrants and ethnic minorities. He has [USN:L1N45U12W TEXT:"escalated"] such rhetoric during the midterm campaign season, particularly against Somali and Muslim Americans including Muslim Democratic US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and Representative Ilhan Omar, a Minnesota Democrat who came to the US as a Somali refugee. Trump repeated his vow that Iran would never get a nuclear weapon, seven months after the United States and Israel launched a war on Tehran aimed in part at crippling its nuclear program. An annual report by the Council on American Islamic Relations released earlier this year [USN:L4N3ZU0AN TEXT:"attributed"] rising Islamophobia in the US in part to Trump's crackdown on immigration and pro-Palestinian protests during his second term.

item.title: Professora lutou contra atirador de escola em Oregon
item.description: Uma professora da escola em Oregon onde um atirador abriu fogo e matou três crianças e um adulto jogou seu celular no agressor, o derrubou e lutou com ele em um ato que salvou vidas, informou a polícia nesta sexta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Herbert Villarraga, Deborah Bloom
item.content:encoded: Uma professora da escola em Oregon onde um atirador abriu fogo e matou três crianças e um adulto jogou seu celular no agressor, o derrubou e lutou com ele em um ato que salvou vidas, informou a polícia nesta sexta-feira. Um dia após o início da investigação sobre o mais recente tiroteio em escola nos EUA, as autoridades divulgaram novos detalhes da cena dentro de uma sala de aula para alunos com necessidades especiais da Escola Primária Silver Rail, onde três crianças de 5, 8 e 11 anos e um adulto foram mortos por um ex-aluno de 16 anos. O chefe de polícia de Bend, Mike Krantz, não identificou a professora que lutou contra o agressor, mas disse em uma coletiva de imprensa que ela jogou seu celular no suspeito, o derrubou e lutou para tirar a espingarda dele. “Ela não ficou ferida nesse incidente, mas quase certamente ajudou a impedir mais derramamento de sangue”, disse Krantz. Enquanto os dois lutavam, um pai entrou na sala de aula e abriu fogo contra o atirador, matando-o. Autoridades informaram que o pai havia seguido o atirador até dentro da escola, após testemunhá-lo disparando uma espingarda do lado de fora do campus. Quando a polícia chegou, três minutos após receber a primeira chamada, o atirador já estava morto, informou a polícia. Antes disso, o agressor de 16 anos, que havia atirado através de portas de vidro trancadas para entrar na escola, havia matado quatro pessoas e ferido outras duas. Ao se referir ao heroísmo demonstrado pela professora que se jogou sobre o suspeito e pelo pai que atirou nele, Krantz disse: “Não acho que possamos subestimar ou menosprezar essa coragem. Quando alguém está disposto a arriscar a própria vida pelos outros, nós reconhecemos isso”. Ele disse que as ações das pessoas que estavam por perto “sem dúvida salvaram vidas” e que “a professora que se dispôs a enfrentar e lutar por seus alunos, isso é verdadeiro heroísmo”. Krantz identificou o atirador como Griffin J. John 2º, que estava armado com uma espingarda calibre 12. Ele disparou cerca de 15 tiros na sala de aula e tinha mais 44 cartuchos consigo. O pai que matou o atirador foi identificado como Kaylub Giamanco, segundo o New York Times. A mãe dele o identificou, relatando que ele é pai de duas meninas que estudam na escola, de acordo com um vídeo publicado pelo New York Times. Moradores de Bend, cidade com cerca de 100 mil habitantes a cerca de 280 km a sudeste de Portland, se reuniram perto da escola para prestar homenagem na manhã desta sexta-feira, colocando flores e velas perto da fita amarela de isolamento que cercava o local do crime. Brooke Olsen, mãe de uma aluna do jardim de infância que se reuniu em segurança com sua família após o tiroteio, também expressou gratidão ao homem que deteve o atirador. “Este é um dia extremamente doloroso e de luto para todos em Bend, especialmente para as famílias da Silver Rail, e precisamos pensar no que vem a seguir em termos de medidas de segurança.” Ataques a tiros em escolas tornaram-se comuns nos EUA, e cada um deles reacende os debates sobre as leis de porte de armas em um país onde o direito de “possuir e portar armas” é protegido pela Segunda Emenda da Constituição. Alguns dos ataques mais mortíferos em escolas nos EUA incluem os ocorridos na Columbine High School em 1999, na Sandy Hook Elementary School em 2012, na Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School em 2018 e na Robb Elementary School em Uvalde, Texas, em 2022.

item.title: Lula vai enviar na próxima semana PEC que zera tarifa do transporte coletivo
item.description: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva deve enviar já na próxima semana -- a última antes da realização do segundo turno da eleição presidencial -- a Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) que garante transporte público urbano gratuito nos finais de semana em todo o país, afirmou nesta sexta-feira o coordenador político da campanha do petista, senador Camilo Santana (PT-CE).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva deve enviar já na próxima semana -- a última antes da realização do segundo turno da eleição presidencial -- a Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) que garante transporte público urbano gratuito nos finais de semana em todo o país, afirmou nesta sexta-feira o coordenador político da campanha do petista, senador Camilo Santana (PT-CE). A ideia, explicou Santana, é utilizar parte da verba destinada a emendas parlamentares para custear as tarifas zero de transporte. "A PEC está pronta e provavelmente o presidente deve encaminhar ao Congresso Nacional na semana que vem", disse a jornalistas. "Claro que a PEC será debatida com os congressistas, onde ele propõe exatamente como o trabalhador vai ter dois dias de descanso, ele possa ter os dois dias do final de semana com transporte gratuito para levar os seus filhos, seus familiares, com lazer, com passeio nesse país onde tiver transporte público", afirmou. O Congresso Nacional aprovou e promulgou nesta semana outra PEC, que põe fim à escala de trabalho 6x1 no Brasil, prevendo novo regime com duas folgas semanais, sendo que uma delas caia preferencialmente no domingo.

item.title: México perfila aprobar proyectos de energía renovable por US$12.500 millones
item.description: El Consejo de Administración de la Comisión Federal de Electricidad tiene previsto votar el 20 de octubre sobre más de 60 proyectos, según una persona con conocimiento del asunto.
item.dc:creator: Michael O'Boyle, Scott Squires
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — La empresa estatal de electricidad de México prevé dar la aprobación preliminar la próxima semana a decenas de proyectos de energía renovable que, en conjunto, producirían suficiente electricidad para rivalizar con ocho reactores nucleares y ayudarían a reforzar la red eléctrica del país, propensa a los apagones. El Consejo de Administración de la Comisión Federal de Electricidad (CFE) tiene previsto votar el 20 de octubre sobre más de 60 proyectos, según una persona con conocimiento del asunto. Las centrales propuestas, en su mayoría parques eólicos y solares, añadirán unos 8,2 gigavatios de capacidad a la red eléctrica mexicana y tendrán un costo estimado de US$12.500 millones, dependiendo de los gastos de transmisión, según la persona, que pidió no ser identificada porque el asunto no es público. Una segunda persona señaló que el número de proyectos que reciban la aprobación definitiva podría ser menor. Un portavoz de la CFE no respondió a una solicitud de comentarios. Ver más: México espera lanzar esquema de financiamiento para proyectos de energía antes de concluir 2026 Los contratos forman parte de la estrategia de la presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum para reforzar la deteriorada red eléctrica de México mediante asociaciones entre empresas privadas y la compañía estatal para construir más infraestructura. La red eléctrica del país ha sufrido apagones estacionales en los últimos años, especialmente en la cálida y húmeda península de Yucatán, debido a que años de falta de inversión han dejado al sistema sin suficientes centrales eléctricas y líneas de transmisión. El impulso a la inversión externa supone un cambio significativo frente a la política del anterior presidente de México, Andrés Manuel López Obrador, quien restringió en gran medida la inversión extranjera en el sector eléctrico. Sin embargo, la legislación mexicana sigue exigiendo que el Estado mantenga al menos 54% de la propiedad de todas las centrales eléctricas. Sheinbaum busca añadir 32 gigavatios de capacidad de generación en México para 2030, de los cuales 40% procederá de fuentes renovables. Lee más en Bloomberg.com

item.title: Anthropic signs lease for first Canadian data center
item.description: Anthropic has signed a lease with EverWind for data center capacity at Point Tupper, Nova Scotia, marking the Claude maker’s first data center agreement in Canada, a company executive said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Anthropic has signed a lease with EverWind for data center capacity at Point Tupper, Nova Scotia, marking the Claude maker’s first data center agreement in Canada, a company executive said on Friday. Here are some more details: Separately, EverWind unveiled plans to invest more than C$10 billion in the data center campus and wind power projects in Nova Scotia, calling it the largest privately funded investment in the province’s history. Data centers have faced criticism over their heavy power and water use and the strain they place on local infrastructure. Jacob Glick, Anthropic’s head of public policy for Canada, said the company would protect ratepayers and water resources while ensuring local communities benefit. Anthropic [USN:L4N4500J8 TEXT:"spent"] $7.33 billion on computing and infrastructure last year, a threefold surge from 2024. The company is preparing for a US IPO that could value it at more than $2 trillion, although New York City Comptroller Mark Levine has [USN:L4N46113W TEXT:"urged"] it to delay the offering over safety and governance concerns.

item.title: Connor Bedard, Blackhawks eye third straight home win vs. Stars
item.description: The Chicago Blackhawks are playing with confidence now that Connor Bedard has returned to the ice.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Chicago Blackhawks are playing with confidence now that Connor Bedard has returned to the ice. Looking to remain undefeated with their fourth-year star in the lineup this season, the Blackhawks also aim to continue their recent home success against the Dallas Stars on Saturday night. Chicago won once in its first six games before its young captain returned from shoulder surgery Tuesday, helping the Blackhawks to a 5-3 victory over Pittsburgh. He recorded an assist in the contest, then added another helper and scored his first goal of the season during Chicago's 4-3 overtime triumph over Winnipeg on Thursday. "We are building on how we want to play, on that identity on how we want to play," Blackhawks coach Jeff Blashill told Chicago Sports Network. Coming off his first 30-goal season, which also produced a career-best 75 points, Bedard has helped the club reset its season this week. He is joined by Blackhawks legend Patrick Kane, who has posted four points in the last four contests. "They've done a real good job of playing off each other," Blashill added. "Kaner is one of the best to ever play. Connor is making his way towards that. He is an elite, elite player in this league." With two assists Thursday, Kane became the all-time leader among American-born players with 895 assists. "We got a little bit of momentum," Kane said. "We want to keep it going." Kane has 77 points in 68 career games against Dallas, while Bedard has recorded five goals and two assists in eight career contests against the Stars. Dallas has won 14 of the last 19 meetings with the Blackhawks. However, three of Chicago's victories came in the last four meetings at the United Center. The Blackhawks have totaled 14 goals and gone 5-for-12 on the power play during their last four home games against Dallas. After dropping their first two games of the season, the Stars are 3-1-1 and recently split a home-and-home series with rival Colorado. After falling 3-2 at home to the Avalanche on Tuesday, Dallas earned a shootout victory by the same score one night later in Denver. "These (close, competitive) games are going to help us moving forward, because they springboard us into a different quadrant of play," Stars coach Glen Gulutzan said. The Stars are 2-1-1 on the road this season. Dallas forward Mikko Rantanen, who recorded an assist Wednesday, has posted six of his team-leading seven points away from home. Rantanen scored in each of his last three games against Chicago and has totaled 39 points in 30 career games against the Blackhawks. Teammate Miro Heiskanen has tallied four of his six points this season over the last three contests. Dallas goaltenders Jake Oettinger (five starts) and Casey DeSmith (two starts) have combined for a 1.71 goals-against average this season. Meanwhile, the Blackhawks are 3-1-0 at home with Spencer Knight in net. He has recorded at least 31 saves in two of those contests. Chicago backup Arvid Soderblom, however, has allowed nine goals on 50 shots in his two starts this season, both on the road. --Field Level Media

item.title: US air traffic controllers to get 2.8% pay raise under FAA deal
item.description: Thousands of US air traffic controllers will get a 2.8% pay raise retroactive to January 1 under a deal announced by the Federal Aviation Administration and a union.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson, Doyinsola Oladipo
item.content:encoded: Thousands of US air traffic controllers will get a 2.8% pay raise retroactive to January 1 under a deal announced by the Federal Aviation Administration and a union. The pay raise, which was authorized by Congress, will be effective October 18 Controllers previously received a 1% raise but the remainder of the $140 million raise was contingent on workforce reforms The agreed changes include tracking of controllers' time, aligning staffing with demand, and improving controller reassignments The FAA has been working to address a persistent shortage of air traffic controllers Many are working mandatory overtime and six-day weeks Local managers and union representatives will now develop shift guidelines based on anticipated workload and operational requirements to ensure more productive controller schedules that maximize coverage during peak traffic hours

item.title: Wings seek home-ice turnaround as Sharks continue road trip
item.description: The Detroit Red Wings began the season with an unusually heavy home schedule. The final game of that stretch comes Saturday night when they host the San Jose Sharks.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Detroit Red Wings began the season with an unusually heavy home schedule. The final game of that stretch comes Saturday night when they host the San Jose Sharks. Detroit opened the season with four straight home games. Following its first road contest, the Red Wings returned for a three-game homestand. They haven't protected home ice particularly well, as their 2-1 victory over winless Philadelphia on Thursday was only their second home win. Defenseman Anton Johansson had a memorable night, scoring his first NHL goal. "It was awesome (to get the win), that was the most important thing," Johansson said. "We've been struggling a little bit with the wins, but I feel we've been playing all right. It's finally nice to get it done." Center Andrew Copp, who contributed just one assist during the first six games, scored the game-winner in the third period. "You're not going to get Grade A chances night after night -- this league is too tight-checking -- but they have to start going in at some point," Copp said. "I've had some good chances and missed my spot by a couple of inches here or there. Then you're kind of fighting it or gripping the stick, so it's good to see one go in, and hopefully we can keep it going." With a four-game road trip looming, the Red Wings could use another win to build momentum. Detroit entered Thursday's game on a three-game skid, including losses in a shootout and overtime. "Even in the three losses, other than Seattle (6-3 defeat), we didn't give up a lot and played pretty decent games," Copp said. "There's just that extra two percent, like in my case not finishing, or getting pucks out or an extra battle at the end.
